question: How should an engineer distinguish a reflow failure from a justified local two-dimensional region, and assess pointer target size/spacing without confusing declarations with measured layout?
selection_reason: Repeated layout and input failures remain uncovered after component and token contracts. The browser limitation must be reflected in evidence labels rather than omitted.
rubric: Preserve task-relevant information and actions at the reflow boundary; do not hide required content to make overflow disappear
Classify two-dimensional exceptions locally with a documented reason, rather than exempting the entire page
Use authoritative target geometry thresholds and retain the named exceptions and input assumptions
Reject malformed, missing, contradictory, or unsupported observations instead of returning a generic accessibility pass
Distinguish synthetic geometry checks, supplied measurements, browser observation, and assistive-technology evidence
Do not turn an observation-model pass into rendered WCAG conformance
Preserve existing Art Direction and component/keyboard responsibilities
evidence_limit: Browser execution remains blocked in this session. Any implementation requiring actual rendering/AT observation stays HOLD; pure geometry or schema checks may receive a narrowly scoped result only.
decision_rule: ACCEPT only a clearly bounded rule with executed tests and independent recheck; unresolved conditions or unavailable runtime evidence HOLD; concrete defects REVISE.
